Carla (AE): FYI mosaic POC — customer reporting slow TTFT and intermittent 429s after a warmup run. They hit it with batch=32 and saw long first-byte lag. Can SE/ops swarm? :grimacing:
Mike (SE): On it. Which model and sequence lengths are they using? Any logs from their client or our side?
Carla (AE): model: open-llm/mosaic-13b, avg seq len ~ 480, peak 1024. They sent a log snippet — our gateway returns 429s ~1m after warmup. They also mentioned "kv prefetch locks" from the client logs.
Mike (SE): Interesting. Two quick things: 1) batch=32 + seq ~1k can cause long batch formation times if continuous batching window is high. 2) If prefetch is enabled on client, simultaneous prefetches can cause KV cache lock contention on a shard and trigger queueing -> perceived TTFT and 429s.
Rahul (ML): Agree. Mosaic's KV cache is sharded; aggressive prefetch across many connections can saturate shard locks. For long seqs, prefer lower batch size (8-16) or enable streaming + smaller batch windows. Also check quantization profile — some FP4 paths increase per-token latency at long context.
Sasha (SRE): Looking at infra metrics for that tenant: I see a spike in per-tenant active requests at t=2034567620 and our per-tenant concurrency guard tripped (429s). They were warmup-ing with 40 parallel clients. That explains the 429s. We can temporarily raise tenant concurrency for the POC but need to coordinate.
Carla (AE): They warmed up with 40 threads to simulate burst. They want consistent TTFT under load. What remediation steps do we recommend now?
Mike (SE): Short term: ask them to reduce parallel warmup to <12 and run a phased warmup (ramp). Also set batch.size=12 and batching.max_delay_ms=10 in client to avoid long formation windows. Example client snippet:
```json
{"batch": {"max_tokens": 2048, "max_requests": 12, "max_delay_ms": 10}, "prefetch": false}
```
Carla (AE): Noted. What about the "kv prefetch locks" callouts?
Rahul (ML): If they need prefetch (cold-starts), use our staged prefetch endpoint `/v1/prefetch` which serializes warmup per-shard. Avoid all-clients prefetch simultaneously. We can also enable background shard warming on their Dedicated node.
Sasha (SRE): I can temporarily increase their concurrency cap to 24 for the next 2 hours while they run a controlled ramp. I'll also watch queue depth. :thumbsup:
DeployBot: deploy-job/infra/wave-12 completed for tenant-mosaic at 2034567700, patch applied: per-tenant-concurrency-window adjustment.
Mike (SE): Also collect a request trace for a slow TTFT request: `X-Request-ID` + `curl -v` to our endpoint and attach trace id. That will show which stage (gateway, router, runtime) spent time.
Carla (AE): Customer asked about pricing if we move them to Dedicated for predictable throughput. Need a ballpark to share now.
Sasha (SRE): Quick ballpark: Dedicated for 1x 8-GPU pod starts at ~ $Xk/month in our quoting model; with pre-warm and higher concurrency expect delta of ~2-3x vs hosted in heavy-burst scenarios. (Need exact quote from Sales Ops.)
Mike (SE): For presales, say "order-of-magnitude": hosted with conservative batch + warmup is usually cheaper for POC, Dedicated is better when sustained concurrency > 200 qps or when SVR/latency SLOs are strict.
Carla (AE): Okay — I'll relay technical fixes: reduce parallel warmup, temp concurrency bump, switch off client prefetch or use `/v1/prefetch`, lower batch size, and provide trace when they reproduce. Also will flag Sales Ops for Dedicated quote.
Rahul (ML): One more note: if they care about first-token latency specifically, suggest enabling KV prefix caching and short-circuit for common prompts; we can add a suggestion list for prompts to pre-cache.
Carla (AE): Great — thanks everyone. I'll coordinate with customer and reopen thread if they re-hit 429/TTFT. :raised_hands:
